boardStatus: The relevant U.S. primary specialty certifier is the American Board of Ophthalmology. Official ABO pages describe general ophthalmology certification after accredited residency via WQE and oral examination. No separate U.S. vitreoretinal fellowship board examination or subspecialty certificate was identified in official ABO materials reviewed (checked 2026-10-07). AUPO FCC compliance is a fellowship training-compliance process, not board certification. The general ophthalmology WQE 2026 outline weights Retina, Vitreous and Intraocular Tumors at 15%; this is not a fellowship-specific exam blueprint.
boardEligibilityNotice: Educational mapping only. This independent course does not confer ABO exam eligibility or board status. ABO eligibility requires applicable accredited ophthalmology residency and current ABO rules; verify directly with ABO. Each institution has its own match, prerequisite, state medical-license and visa requirements; do not infer universal eligibility from this course. MEE page says applicants must be eligible for a full Massachusetts medical license. Wilmer page enumerates separate IMG prerequisites only.
